name: EPIC 201408013
description: A red giant in K2 campaign 1, 10.4 solar radii and 0.88 solar masses, weighed by its oscillations.

radius.source: Khan et al. (2023), A&A 677, A21, k2_apo, EPIC 201408013 (K2 campaign 1): PARAM radius (solar radii) 10.354075 (16th-84th percentiles 9.862447-10.867117), MA09 pipeline with APOGEE DR17

mass.source: Khan et al. (2023), A&A 677, A21, k2_apo, EPIC 201408013 (K2 campaign 1): PARAM mass (solar masses) 0.883376 (16th-84th percentiles 0.775161-1.002481), MA09 pipeline with APOGEE DR17

temperature.source: Khan et al. (2023), A&A 677, A21, k2_apo, EPIC 201408013: APOGEE DR17 effective temperature 4927.5073 +/- 50 K (the catalogue's final uncertainty)

distance.source: Khan et al. (2023), A&A 677, A21, k2_apo, EPIC 201408013 (K2 campaign 1): PARAM asteroseismic distance (pc) 4897.851562 (16th-84th percentiles 4705.507812-5086.484375), MA09 pipeline with APOGEE DR17

color.reason: PARAM fits an extinction A_V = 0.03 mag toward this star (Khan et al. (2023), A&A 677, A21, k2_apo, AV-M), and the color routes do not remove extinction; APOGEE measured its temperature

text.card: A red giant 4,898 parsecs away, 10 times the Sun's width, weighed by its starquakes.
text.introduction: Its oscillations, recorded in K2 campaign 1, give 0.88 solar masses and 10.4 solar radii; APOGEE spectra give 4,928 K at its surface.
